statement: Solve $\\frac{dy}{dx}+2y=e^{-x}$ with $y(0)=1$, and verify your solution satisfies the equation and the initial condition.
solution: Integrating factor $\\mu=e^{\\int 2dx}=e^{2x}$. Then $\\frac{d}{dx}(e^{2x}y)=e^{x}$, so $e^{2x}y=e^{x}+C$, giving $y=e^{-x}+Ce^{-2x}$. With $y(0)=1$: $1=1+C\\Rightarrow C=0$, so $y=e^{-x}$. Check: $y'=-e^{-x}$ and $-e^{-x}+2e^{-x}=e^{-x}$; also $y(0)=1$.
